glance: SHASTA-3/4 (NEJM): plozasiran cut triglycerides and acute pancreatitis (1 vs 5 per 100 patient-years) in severe hypertriglyceridemia.

PROGRESS (NEJM): transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) beat surveillance in moderate aortic stenosis with at-risk features (16.7% vs 23.9% death or heart failure (HF) event at 2 years), driven by HF events.

SIMPLAAFY (JAMA): after left atrial appendage closure (LAAC), aspirin alone and reduced-dose non-vitamin K oral anticoagulant (NOAC) were both noninferior to dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) at 6 months.

American Thoracic Society (ATS) guideline: strong recommendations for as-needed inhaled corticosteroid (ICS)-containing relievers at National Asthma Education and Prevention Program (NAEPP) steps 1-2 and ICS-formoterol maintenance-and-reliever therapy (MART) at steps 3-5.

Neutral or negative: hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate in contemporary heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) (H-HeFT), conservative kidney management vs dialysis preparation in frail older adults (no quality-adjusted life-year (QALY) difference).

Ertapenem-resistant, meropenem-susceptible Enterobacterales: higher 30-day mortality on imipenem or meropenem (odds ratio (OR) 2.24), challenging Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) guidance.

top.title: Plozasiran in severe hypertriglyceridemia (SHASTA-3 and SHASTA-4, NEJM)
bullets: 757 adults, 2:1 to plozasiran 25 mg or placebo at baseline and months 3, 6, 9.
Placebo-adjusted triglyceride change at 12 months: -45 and -47 percentage points; triglycerides below 500 mg/dL in 91% and 93% vs 51% and 50%.
Pooled acute pancreatitis: 1 vs 5 per 100 patient-years (rate ratio 0.22; P = 0.008).
top.caveat: Funded by Arrowhead; primary end point is triglyceride change; pancreatitis from a pooled analysis over 12 months.

top.title: PROGRESS: transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) vs clinical surveillance in moderate aortic stenosis (NEJM)
bullets: 744 patients with moderate aortic stenosis (AS) and at least one at-risk feature; mean age 78 years, mean valve area 1.2 cm2.
Death or heart failure (HF) event at 2 years: 16.7% vs 23.9% (risk difference -7.2 points, 95% confidence interval (CI) -13.1 to -1.3).
Death 8.4% vs 7.3%; HF events 10.8% vs 19.0%.
top.caveat: Open-label; funded by Edwards Lifesciences; benefit driven by HF events, which are open to ascertainment bias; no mortality difference.

top.title: SIMPLAAFY: antithrombotic therapy after left atrial appendage closure (JAMA)
bullets: 1857 patients, 1:1:1 to dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) 6 months, reduced-dose non-vitamin K oral anticoagulant (NOAC) 3 months, or aspirin alone 12 months.
6-month death, stroke, embolism or major bleeding: 6.9% DAPT vs 5.1% NOAC (relative risk (RR) 0.75) vs 3.3% aspirin (RR 0.49); both noninferior.
Device-related thrombus 3.4%, 0.9%, and 2.7%.
top.caveat: Open-label; 6-month follow-up; uncomplicated left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) only; bleeding and thrombus outcomes exploratory.

guidelines.title: As-needed inhaled corticosteroids in asthma (clinical practice guideline)
bullets: Six population, intervention, comparison, outcome (PICO) questions, Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE); adolescents and adults across National Asthma Education and Prevention Program (NAEPP) steps 1-5.
Steps 1-2: strong for as-needed-only inhaled corticosteroid (ICS)-short-acting beta2-agonist (SABA) or ICS-formoterol over SABA only; conditional over scheduled ICS plus as-needed SABA.

Steps 3-5: strong for ICS-formoterol maintenance-and-reliever therapy (MART) over scheduled ICS-long-acting beta2-agonist (LABA) plus as-needed SABA; conditional for ICS+SABA reliever over SABA reliever on scheduled ICS-LABA.

guidelines.title: Diagnosis and management of hepatitis delta virus infection
bullets: Test every hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)-positive person at least once for hepatitis delta virus (HDV) antibody; confirm with HDV RNA.
Elastography-based fibrosis assessment; labs and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) surveillance every 6 months.
Compensated chronic HDV viremia: bulevirtide for suppression, or bulevirtide plus pegylated interferon (peg-IFN) alfa-2a for a finite course.

guidelines.title: Kidney end points in anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis
bullets: Expert proposal for standardized definitions: active kidney disease, response, refractory disease, remission, relapse, recovery, kidney failure.
Research agenda; Delphi consensus to follow.

guidelines.issuer: ESCP / UEG / ESGAR / EAGEN / ESGENA / ESNM / ESPCG
guidelines.title: Multidisciplinary management of obstructed defecation syndrome
bullets: 28 statements: 1 moderate, 2 low, 3 very low certainty, 22 expert opinion.
Conservative treatment first; biofeedback before surgery when dyssynergia and diet and laxatives fail.
Surgery only for selected persistent cases after multidisciplinary pelvic floor evaluation.

guidelines.title: Management of Crohn's disease in adults
bullets: Adaptation and update of the 2020 Colombian guideline; Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE).
52 recommendations across 7 questions: relapse prediction, conventional and advanced therapy, perianal fistulizing disease, surgical-endoscopic approach, postoperative recurrence.

guidelines.title: Continuous glucose monitoring in primary care
bullets: Delphi of 58 primary care professionals.
Covers indication, prescription, initiation, monitoring, and discontinuation within shared decision-making.

items.title: Plozasiran for severe hypertriglyceridemia (SHASTA-3, SHASTA-4)
bullets: Median triglyceride reduction from baseline 79% and 81%; placebo-adjusted -45 and -47 points.
Acute pancreatitis 1 vs 5 per 100 patient-years (rate ratio 0.22).
Adverse events 73% in both groups.
items.caveat: Industry-funded; 12 months; see Top 3.

items.title: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) in moderate aortic stenosis with at-risk features (PROGRESS)
bullets: n=744; 45.6% low surgical risk.
Death or heart failure (HF) event at 2 years 16.7% vs 23.9%.
HF events 10.8% vs 19.0%; death 8.4% vs 7.3%.
items.caveat: Industry-funded; open-label; composite driven by HF events.

items.title: Antithrombotic therapy after left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) (SIMPLAAFY)
bullets: n=1857; mean CHA2DS2-VASc 4.2.
Primary composite 6.9% dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT), 5.1% reduced-dose non-vitamin K oral anticoagulant (NOAC), 3.3% aspirin.
Major bleeding 4.5%, 2.7%, 1.7%.
items.caveat: 6-month follow-up; secondary outcomes not multiplicity-adjusted.

items.title: Coronary CT angiography (CCTA)-guided vs intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) (P4)
bullets: n=1105; CT-derived fractional flow reserve (FFR-CT) 0.80 or less.
Target-vessel failure at 12 months 4.1% vs 4.6% (risk difference -0.42 points, 95% confidence interval (CI) -2.82 to 1.99); noninferior, not superior.
Procedural complications 6 vs 9 patients.
items.caveat: Funded by GE HealthCare and Heartflow; margin 4.5 points against low event rates; 12 months.

items.title: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) plus guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) vs GDMT alone in severe pure aortic regurgitation (SEASON-AR)
bullets: n=210, high or prohibitive surgical risk, 18 Chinese centers.
Death, disabling stroke or heart failure (HF) rehospitalization at 1 year 8.3% vs 24.8% (hazard ratio (HR) 0.31).
HF rehospitalization 3.7% vs 21.3%; more major bleeding and new pacemakers with TAVR.
items.caveat: Small; open-label; single device (VitaFlow); 1-year follow-up.

items.title: Hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate in contemporary heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) (H-HeFT)
bullets: n=592, 23 Danish hospitals, mean follow-up 3.7 years.
Primary composite 30.6% vs 30.5% (hazard ratio (HR) 0.90, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.67-1.21).
items.caveat: Predominantly White population; not powered for mortality.

items.title: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) vs coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) for left main disease, long-term (IRIS-MAIN)
bullets: 5379 Asian patients; median follow-up 10.0 years.
10-year mortality 24.0% vs 22.9% (overlap-weighted hazard ratio (HR) 1.00, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.87-1.14).
items.caveat: Non-randomized; CI does not exclude benefit or harm.

items.title: Vutrisiran in transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTR) cardiomyopathy through month 48 (HELIOS-B open-label extension (OLE))
bullets: 466 entered the extension.
Continuous vs delayed vutrisiran: first cardiovascular (CV) event or death hazard ratio (HR) 0.63; death HR 0.63.
Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire overall summary (KCCQ-OS) difference 9.0; N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) ratio 0.66.
items.caveat: Comparison of early vs delayed start, not randomized after the parent trial.

items.title: Single vs double ProGlide closure after transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) (SINGLE-CLOSURE)
bullets: n=876, 25 Chinese centers.
Access-site vascular complications 13.1% vs 15.1% (difference -2.2%); noninferior.
Major vascular complications 0.5% vs 1.4%; extra closure devices 2.5% vs 0.9%.
items.caveat: Events mostly minor; in-hospital end point only.

items.title: Transseptal transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) with SAPIEN M3 (ENCIRCLE)
bullets: 299 treated; mitral regurgitation (MR) 1+ or less in 97.0% at 2 years.
Death or heart failure (HF) hospitalization 35.6% (death 25.1%).
Disabling stroke 6.6%, valve thrombosis 7.1%, hemolysis requiring intervention 7.6%.
items.caveat: No control arm; outcomes in survivors.

items.title: PREVENT-HF equations by heart failure (HF) subtype
bullets: Pooled cohorts n=23,652 plus two electronic health record (EHR) samples (29,815 and 138,999).
area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) 0.824-0.897 vs heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) 0.789-0.833.
Calibration similar for both subtypes.
items.caveat: Equations not built for subtype prediction; thresholds not established.

items.title: Conservative kidney management vs dialysis preparation in frail older adults (Prepare for Kidney Care)
bullets: n=445, median age 82, 31 UK centers, mean follow-up 4.5 years.
quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs) 1.354 vs 1.472 (adjusted difference -0.147, 95% confidence interval (CI) -0.350 to 0.056).
Dialysis access complications lower with responsive management (incidence rate ratio (IRR) 0.41); deaths 69% vs 63%.
items.caveat: Only 7% of screened patients randomized; harms not prespecified.

items.title: Ectopic Cushing syndrome outcomes
bullets: n=1463; 57.1% metastatic; median follow-up 57 months.
Cushing-related death 13.4%; infection 31.7%; venous thromboembolism (VTE) 8.5%.
Complete biochemical remission within 6 months: lower late complications (adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 0.55) and Cushing-related mortality (0.49).
items.caveat: Retrospective; investigator-adjudicated cause of death.

items.title: Body mass index (BMI)-specific waist circumference and incident type 2 diabetes in older women (Women's Health Initiative (WHI))
bullets: n=133,620 WHI women; validated in Health and Retirement Study (HRS) and Healthy Aging in Neighborhoods of Diversity across the Life Span (HANDLS).
Joint body mass index and waist circumference (BMI-WC) categories hazard ratios (HRs) 1.40-4.43.
C-statistics about 0.60-0.75.
items.caveat: Women only; modest individual discrimination.

items.title: Sex hormones and muscle and function in men aged 78-97
bullets: n=477; 247 with 6-year follow-up.
Higher total testosterone linked to higher deuterated creatine dilution (D3Cr) muscle mass and less decline in grip strength, walk speed, and chair stands.
items.caveat: Observational; single hormone measurement; attrition.

items.title: Elafibranor for alkaline phosphatase (ALP) normalization in primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) with ALP above 1 to below 1.67x upper limit of normal (ULN) (ELSPIRE)
bullets: ALP normalization 85.3% vs 23.3% (difference 62.0%).
ALP change -36.5% vs -4.2%.
items.caveat: Small; biochemical surrogate end point; 1 year.

items.title: Smartphone-enabled physician-supervised treat-to-target for gout
bullets: 280 men, 12 months.
serum urate (SUA) below 360 umol/L: 85.0% vs 48.6% (relative risk (RR) 1.75).
Flares 0.02 vs 0.10 per year.
items.caveat: Single center; men only; open-label.

items.title: Ethnicity and response to treatment escalation in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)
bullets: n=422; major clinical response at 12 months 23% overall.
Black 10% vs White 24%; adjusted odds ratio (OR) 0.13 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.02-0.88).
items.caveat: Observational; small subgroups; wide CI; industry co-funding.

items.title: Pre-COPD score to predict incident chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
bullets: Derived in Copenhagen General Population Study (CGPS) (n=14,506); validated in Copenhagen City Heart Study (CCHS) and COPDGene.
10-year incidence in CGPS 1.5%, 9.3%, 24%, 42% across risk categories.
area under the curve (AUC) 0.88, 0.76, 0.81.
items.caveat: Pre-bronchodilator spirometry definitions; mostly Danish populations.

items.title: Dupilumab and lung function in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) with type 2 inflammation (BOREAS, NOTUS)
bullets: Pre-bronchodilator forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) +83 mL vs placebo; post-bronchodilator +71 mL.
Greater effect with higher eosinophils or fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO).
items.caveat: Post hoc; spirometric outcomes only.

items.title: Desaturation-based sleep apnea scoring in Black individuals
bullets: Black participants: about 20% fewer airflow events met the 4% desaturation criterion (ratio 0.79 and 0.80).
Heart-rate-response apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) linked to major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) or mortality in both cohorts (hazard ratio (HR) 1.33 and 1.26).
items.caveat: Observational; self-identified race as proxy for pigmentation.

items.title: Imipenem-cilastatin-funobactam vs imipenem-relebactam in hospital-acquired bacterial pneumonia (HABP) and ventilator-associated bacterial pneumonia (VABP)
bullets: n=449, 62 hospitals (58 in China).
14-day mortality 3.0% vs 2.7% (difference 0.2%, 95% confidence interval (CI) -3.5 to 4.0).
Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events (AEs) 7% vs 11%.
items.caveat: Industry-funded; low mortality relative to 10% margin.

items.title: Imipenem or meropenem for ertapenem-resistant Enterobacterales
bullets: n=374; 36% ertapenem-resistant, carbapenemase-negative.
30-day mortality higher with ertapenem resistance (odds ratio (OR) 2.24, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.26-3.98).
Porin alterations and extra beta-lactamase genes enriched.
items.caveat: Observational, weighted comparison; residual confounding possible.

items.title: Shoulder injury after COVID-19 vs influenza vaccination (shoulder injury related to vaccine administration (SIRVA))
bullets: 1,901,588 vaccinations at Kaiser Permanente Southern California.
1.84 vs 1.15 per 10,000 (adjusted relative risk (RR) 1.63; +0.67 per 10,000).
Age 65 or older vs high-dose influenza: RR 1.41 (0.92-2.15).
items.caveat: Natural language processing (NLP)-based case finding; single health system; one season.

items.title: Timing of long COVID improvement
bullets: n=1019 with likely long COVID at 12 months.
Primary improvement 36.2% by 24 months, 50.1% by 36 months.
Long COVID Research Index (LCRI) to 0 in 26.9% by 36 months.
items.caveat: Observational; no causal inference.

items.title: KIT D816V-selective tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) in systemic mastocytosis with associated myeloid neoplasm
bullets: Overall survival 37.9 vs 17.8 months.
36-month acute myeloid leukemia (AML) transformation 5.9% vs 27.1%.
items.caveat: Observational; treatment selection bias; abstract is a brief summary.

items.title: SER-155 live biotherapeutic in allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) recipients
bullets: Randomized cohort 45; 34 transplanted (20 SER-155, 14 placebo).
Safety comparable to placebo; engraftment of 16 of 16 strains.
Bloodstream infection 10.0% vs 43% (odds ratio (OR) 0.15, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.01-1.13); other efficacy end points not significant.
items.caveat: Phase 1b safety trial; bloodstream infection (BSI) is a secondary end point with a CI crossing 1.

method: Source: PubMed E-utilities, entry date within the last 7 days. Query A: 30 internal medicine and subspecialty journals. Query B: publication type Practice Guideline or Guideline in internal medicine topics. Duplicates removed by PMID.
Screening and summaries: Claude, from abstracts and metadata only. Numbers are copied from abstracts; open the linked record before citing.
Full text: PMC records exist for 4 of 124 candidates. A PMC record does not guarantee machine-readable full text.

Excluded by scope: oncology, neurology and stroke, pediatrics (including the KALUMI malaria trial), surgery-only, health policy, narrative and opinion pieces. ACP Journal Club synopses in Annals were skipped because they carry no abstract.
Not searched: preprints, society websites without PubMed indexing (ACC, ESC, KDIGO, IDSA, ADA living updates), FDA actions.
Badges describe the result against the primary end point: Positive, Negative, Neutral (no clear difference), Descriptive (observational, uncontrolled, or no efficacy test).
